edges.note: France put the file in a civil science agency with a public archive and it is still running; Britain kept it in a defence secretariat with no project name and closed it. Reasoning: contrasting institutional siting and survival of the two arrangements over the same period.

edges.label: 2025 Canadian recommendation versus the 2009 British closure
edges.note: Canada in 2025 recommends building the standing public UAP service that Britain abolished in 2009 and that Pope spent the intervening years arguing should not have been abolished. Reasoning: the two governments moved in opposite directions on the same question sixteen years apart.

timeline.label: Smith writes the 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum
timeline.text: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith, Senior Radio Engineer of the Canadian Department of Transport, writes a Top Secret memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications recording what he had been told in Washington: that the flying saucer question was the most highly classified subject in the United States government, rating higher than the H-bomb, and was being worked by a small group headed by Vannevar Bush. Library and Archives Canada quotes the same memorandum's operative line: 'the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence'.

timeline.label: Project Magnet approved
timeline.text: The Canadian Department of Transport approves Smith's request. Project Magnet is the first government programme anywhere whose stated purpose includes applying recovered UAP data to practical engineering.

timeline.label: UK Flying Saucer Working Party reports
timeline.text: Britain's first official body on the question reports and recommends no further investigation - the same self-terminating conclusion Project Condign would reach in 2000.

timeline.label: Project Magnet report recommends acquiring the technology
timeline.text: Smith's report concludes that 'we are forced to the conclusion that the vehicles are probably extra-terrestrial, in spite of our prejudices to the contrary' and recommends 'a substantial effort towards the acquisition of as much as possible of this technology, which would without doubt be of great value to us'.

timeline.label: Project Second Storey established
timeline.text: The Defence Research Board establishes a committee under NRC astronomer Peter Millman. It builds a standardised report form with a weighting factor to minimise the 'personal equation', meets six times, concludes UFOs are neither a security threat nor of scientific interest, and recommends ending all Canadian military investigation.

timeline.label: Canada-US joint UFO reporting system
timeline.text: Library and Archives Canada records that an agreement was finalised between the United States and Canada to institute a joint reporting system for UFOs under CIRVIS/MERINT, 'to extend the early warning coverage for the defence of North America'. Posters depicted a saucer-like object alongside missiles and submarines as examples of objects to be reported.

timeline.label: Chile's first official UAP circular
timeline.text: Colonel Sergio Bravo Flores, Director of the Chilean Meteorological Office, sends the first official circular to 43 aeronautical installations from Arica to the Chilean Antarctic Territory requesting reports. Part of the resulting dozen reports are forwarded to the University of Colorado, where the Condon Committee is working.

timeline.label: IHEDN committee opens the French file
timeline.text: A committee of the Institut des Hautes Études de Défense Nationale chaired by General Blanchard of the Gendarmerie Nationale opens the unidentified flying objects file with the objective of proposing how to organise research and data collection. Its recommendations are adopted.

timeline.label: GEPAN created inside CNES
timeline.text: The French national space agency establishes GEPAN under Claude Poher with the authority of director general Yves Sillard - the world's first and still only permanent civilian government UAP office with a public case archive. The Gendarmerie Nationale routes sighting reports to it by teletype.

timeline.label: Operação Prato begins on Colares
timeline.text: The Brazilian Air Force and the National Information Service open the first Brazilian military operation mounted solely to investigate UAP, at the request of the mayor of Colares after residents report burns and puncture wounds from descending lights. Captain Uyrangê Hollanda commands.

timeline.label: The Petrozavodsk phenomenon
timeline.text: A luminous object is reported from Copenhagen and Helsinki to Vladivostok. Northern European governments write to the president of the USSR Academy of Sciences asking whether it was Soviet weapons testing. The Academy's own preliminary report concludes that 'based on the available data, it is unfeasible to satisfactorily understand the observed phenomenon'.

timeline.label: Founding meeting of SETKA at the USSR Academy of Sciences
timeline.text: Migulin and Platov of IZMIRAN, Narimanov and Petrovskaya of the Institute for Space Studies, Balashov and Volga of secret military unit 67947, Gindilis of the Shternberg Institute and others meet. SETKA-AN and SETKA-MO are established on the order of the Military-Industrial Commission. The official history later gives as one reason for secrecy the possibility 'that some of the UFO characteristics could be used for military purposes'.

timeline.label: GEPAN's classified five-volume report
timeline.text: GEPAN reports to its scientific council in five volumes and about 500 pages, limited to 120 or 140 copies and secret. Of eleven high-strangeness cases studied by four-person teams including psychologists, ten were concluded to be material phenomena not explicable as natural or human. A document in the US NSA's declassified UFO collection assesses that its method makes 'the bulk of the Condon Report seem very poor by comparison'.

timeline.label: Soviet Navy anomalous phenomena reporting instruction
timeline.text: Guidelines for the Soviet Navy on collecting anomalous phenomena data are signed by the Deputy Commander of the Main Headquarters of the Navy, Vice Admiral Saakyan.

timeline.label: The Brazilian 'Night of the UFOs'
timeline.text: Twenty-one unidentified radar plots over four Brazilian states. Five Brazilian Air Force fighters are scrambled from Santa Cruz and Anápolis. One Mirage closes to two miles of a contact that zigzags and then accelerates away from a supersonic interceptor; the pilot later estimates Mach 15. Thirteen plots appear astern of an F-5 which turns 180 degrees and sees nothing.

timeline.label: Moreira Lima's press conference
timeline.text: At 16:30 the Brazilian Minister of Aeronautics convenes the press with the five intercept pilots and the air traffic controllers and says: 'It is not a question of believing or not believing. We can only give technical information. There are several hypotheses. Technically, I would tell you gentlemen that we have no explanation.' He promises a full dossier within thirty days. It never appears.

timeline.label: Brazilian Air Defence Command records solid, intelligent objects
timeline.text: Brigadier José Pessoa Cavalcanti de Albuquerque signs a CONFIDENCIAL Relatório de Ocorrências concluding that 'the phenomena are solid and reflect in a certain manner intelligence, by the capacity to follow and to maintain distance from observers as well as to fly in formation, not necessarily crewed'. It stays classified for twenty-three years.

timeline.label: The Varginha encounter
timeline.text: Three young women in Varginha, Minas Gerais report a crouching creature with red eyes and three fingers; a week earlier an ultralight pilot reported a cylindrical craft coming down outside the town. Rumours of military recovery and of an American removal follow. A 2010 Brazilian military inquiry attributes the sighting to a mentally disabled man and routine vehicle movements.

timeline.label: CEFAA created in Chile
timeline.text: Gonzalo Miranda Aguirre, Director of Chile's Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil, creates the Comité de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos after a sighting wave over Arica and the expressed interest of the former Air Force Commander-in-Chief. Ricardo Bermúdez takes the directorship and holds it until 2016.

timeline.label: COMETA publishes 'Les OVNI et la Défense'
timeline.text: A committee of French retired general officers, weapons engineers, an admiral and a national police chief, almost all IHEDN auditors, concludes that the physical reality of unknown flying objects is 'almost certain', that 'a single hypothesis sufficiently takes into account the facts ... the hypothesis of extraterrestrial visitors', and recommends that France 'initiate diplomatic demarches to the United States ... to urge the superpower to collaborate and, if necessary, exert useful pressure'.

timeline.label: Project Condign reports
timeline.text: The UK Defence Intelligence Staff completes 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region' as Scientific & Technical Memorandum 55/2/00. Its key recommendation is that DI55 should no longer monitor UAP reports; its paragraph on 'Related Military Applications' is withheld under the defence exemption; its chapter on other countries denies any US or Canadian collaboration 'of any sort' and then redacts four lines.

timeline.label: Condign released under FOI
timeline.text: The Ministry of Defence releases the Condign report following a September 2005 Freedom of Information Act request by David Clarke and Gary Anthony. The publication scheme entry names the Directorate of Air Staff as author organisation.

timeline.label: The National Archives UFO release programme begins
timeline.text: The first of ten tranches of MoD UFO files is published at nationalarchives.gov.uk/ufos with a highlights guide by David Clarke. The programme runs to June 2013 and covers DEFE 24 and DEFE 31.

timeline.label: Brazil declassifies the 1986 report
timeline.text: The Air Defence Command report of 2 June 1986 is released to the Arquivo Nacional. The Brazilian Air Force begins transferring its whole UAP holding to the National Archives; by 2022 it is the second most consulted collection there, behind only the records of the military dictatorship.

timeline.label: The MoD closes the UFO desk
timeline.text: Britain terminates its public UAP reporting channel with effect from December 2009, in the same period in which it was handling the largest volume of sighting reports in thirty years. The National Archives records that the closure 'sparked' a disclosure campaign.

timeline.label: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR case
timeline.text: A Chilean Navy helicopter films an object in daylight on infrared during a coastal patrol. Two radar stations cannot see it although they can see the helicopters; air traffic control confirms no authorised aircraft in the area. CEFAA analyses the case for two years.

timeline.label: Chile releases the Navy footage
timeline.text: CEFAA publishes the Chilean Navy infrared video without an explanation - the first release of state military sensor footage of an unresolved object by a Latin American government, three years before the US Department of Defense authorised release of the three Navy videos.

timeline.label: CEFAA becomes SEFAA
timeline.text: By Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385 the Chilean office is moved in the DGAC organisation chart to the Subdepartamento Comunicacional and renamed the Sección de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos.

timeline.label: Canada's Sky Canada Project reports
timeline.text: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada publishes 'Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in Canada', recommending that a federal lead be identified and a dedicated service established to collect testimony, investigate and publish, and that Canada partner with AARO and NASA, GEIPAN and SEFAA. It is the first G7 report of the 2020s to name which foreign arrangements it would copy.

timeline.label: Varginha witnesses brief three members of Congress
timeline.text: In Rep. Tim Burchett's office, neurosurgeon Ítalo Venturelli, forensic pathologist Armando Fortunato and ultralight pilot Carlos de Sousa brief Burchett, Anna Paulina Luna and Eric Burlison. Five days later a National Press Club conference follows, at which retired USAF Colonel Fred Claussen sets out the Air Mobility Command paperwork trail any American retrieval flight would have generated and appeals to participants to come forward.

timeline.label: Nick Pope dies
timeline.text: The only person to have run Britain's MoD UFO desk and then spent thirty years describing it dies at home aged 60, two months after disclosing a stage 4 oesophageal cancer diagnosis and writing of 'the secrets I've been privy to'. Obituaries follow in The Telegraph, The Times, The Economist and The New York Times.

timeline.label: The US release reaches the allies
timeline.text: More than 160 UAP files are published on the US Department of Defense website. Within days Kyodo News reports that the footage shows a football-shaped object near Japan, The Japan Times reports Tokyo analysing the trove, and the Buenos Aires Times reports that the release documents the 31 July 1995 Aerolíneas Argentinas Bariloche encounter in a section on investigations conducted outside the United States - citing the 1999 French COMETA report as a source.

timeline.label: Japan confirms it holds UAP footage
timeline.text: Following its review of the US release, coverage reports that the Japanese government has confirmed possession of UAP footage taken near Japanese airspace and that Japan will release files of its own. Japan has no standing UAP office of the GEIPAN or SEFAA kind.

timeline.label: GEIPAN's forty-ninth-year figures
timeline.text: GEIPAN reports more than 9,897 testimonies representing about 5,170 observation cases in 49 years, with 3,336 published; 66.5 per cent classed A or B, 30.3 per cent class C for lack of data, and 3.2 per cent class D - unexplained after investigation.

timeline.label: Congress asks the FBI and CIA about Varginha
timeline.text: NewsNation reports that a lawmaker - contemporaneous coverage names Rep. Eric Burlison - has asked the FBI and the CIA for information on the Varginha case, six months after the Brazilian witnesses testified on Capitol Hill.

entityInfo.throughLine: Every national record on this board contains the same two moves in sequence: a classified assessment that the objects are real and structured, and an official recommendation to stop looking. Britain's Condign said UAP 'regularly appear in the UKADR' and then recommended DI55 stop monitoring them. Canada's Project Magnet said the vehicles were 'probably extra-terrestrial' and recommended acquiring the technology, and was defunded two years later. Brazil's Air Defence Command said the phenomena were 'solid and reflect intelligence' and classified the finding for twenty-three years. The USSR ran two programmes and gave as a reason for their secrecy that the characteristics might be militarily exploitable. Only France and Chile built offices that publish, and in June 2025 the Government of Canada named those two - and the American AARO - as the only models worth copying.

gaps: The exact Library and Archives Canada file citation for Wilbert Smith's 21 November 1950 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum was not confirmed. LAC's own exhibition quotes the memorandum and dates it but cites only the Defence Research Board file (RG 24, acc. 83-84/167, box 7523, file DRBS 3800-10-1, pt.1) for Project Magnet material. Researchers commonly place the Department of Transport memorandum in RG 97. Until the DOT file reference is confirmed at LAC, the famous four-point passage ('rating higher even than the H-bomb'; 'Flying saucers exist'; 'a small group headed by Doctor Vannevar Bush'; 'of tremendous significance') must remain tier 2. This is the single highest-value verification task on this board.

The four redacted lines following Condign Volume 3 paragraph 12's denial of any UK-US-Canada intelligence exchange 'of any sort' have never been contested by FOI review. A fresh request specifically for that paragraph, and for paragraph 7 'Related Military Applications' and paragraph 6 'Radar Detection of Plasmas', is the obvious next British action.

The English translation of the COMETA conclusion circulating since 1999 renders the key sentence as 'The extraterrestrial hypothesis is far from the best scientific hypothesis', which contradicts the paragraph immediately above it and the widely reported French sense. The original French text of 'Les OVNI et la Défense' must be obtained and the sentence collated. Press coverage in August 2026 rendered the same conclusion as 'by far the best'.

Nick Pope's precise MoD post title, grade and division designation were never confirmed from a primary MoD document, and he died on 6 April 2026. The paywalled obituaries in The Telegraph (10 April 2026), The Times (15 April 2026), The Economist (16 April 2026) and The New York Times (28 April 2026) should be read; any personal papers should be traced before they disperse.

The Operação Prato file at the Arquivo Nacional has not been worked page by page in this pass. The official negative finding and Captain Uyrangê Hollanda's 1997 interview cannot both be true; the file is the arbiter. The exact date of Hollanda's death and whether any inquest was held are also unestablished.

The 30-day dossier promised by Brazilian Minister of Aeronautics Octávio Moreira Lima on 23 May 1986 never appeared publicly. Whether one was written and withheld is a specific, answerable question for the Arquivo Nacional.

The photographic negatives taken by press photographer Adenir Britto on 19 May 1986 were collected a month later by two officers of the Brazilian Aerospace Technical Centre accompanied by the American researcher James J. Hurtak, on the stated basis that NASA would analyse them, and were never returned. Their present location is unknown and is a live custody question.

Spain's sixty-six released Ministry of Defence UFO files are recorded inside Project Condign but have not been located or worked here. The Ejército del Aire's own archival references and the release dates need to be established.

No primary Russian-language archival citation for the SETKA founding documents, the 18 October 1978 Academy of Sciences meeting minutes, or the Military-Industrial Commission order was obtained. The best available source remains a secondary English-language account by Stonehill and Mantle. The relationship between 'Institute 22', SETKA-AN, SETKA-MO, Galaktika, Gorizont and secret military unit 67947 needs to be resolved from Russian sources.

The term 'Thirteenth Department', used in the literature for a Soviet General Staff unit handling anomalous phenomena, could not be tied to any documented body in this pass and has deliberately not been asserted. Military unit 67947, named in the SETKA account, is the concrete institutional lead to follow.

Japan's May 2026 statements were established from Kyodo News, Japan Times and other headlines indexed through Google News; the article bodies could not be retrieved (paywall and bot protection). The Japanese Ministry of Defense's own statements, and whether Japan has committed to a file release, need to be sourced directly from Japanese-language government material.
Peru's Air Force UAP office (variously OIFAA and DIFAA) is a placeholder. Its founding instrument, current name, reporting line, case output and whether it publishes findings are all unestablished.
Argentina has no entity on this board beyond the 1995 Bariloche case. The Comisión de Estudio de Fenómenos Aeroespaciales within the Fuerza Aérea Argentina, and any successor, need to be researched.

No NATO institutional position on UAP was located. The alliance appears in this record only indirectly, through Condign's reference to 'other NATO nations' and through the bilateral behaviour of member states. Whether NATO has ever issued guidance, and whether the subject has appeared in a NAC or Military Committee document, is unanswered.

The exact CEFAA case reference and the Chilean Navy's own report on the November 2014 helicopter FLIR case were not located; the account here rests on January 2017 press reporting. SEFAA's resolved-case archive should be searched for the file.
Whether the Government of Canada has designated a lead department in response to the Sky Canada Project's June 2025 recommendations, as at August 2026, is unestablished.
